Include: the game title, a short mission-briefing panel, a prominent START button, a row of upgrade options (Damage / Fire Rate / Speed) as menu buttons, and a HUD-style header (wave / HP / credits). Put strong emphasis on the visual design: a beautiful, cohesive sci-fi home screen with a distinct identity, strong layout, color and typography. Make this screen look genuinely polished.

history.critique: BRIEF & INTENT: Two required elements fail the visible composition. (1) The mandatory row of upgrade menu buttons (Damage / Fire Rate / Speed) is absent from the frame entirely — the briefing text mentions them but no clickable menu exists, so a core deliverable is omitted, not just under-polished. (2) The primary START button is clipped at the bottom edge (only its top border and partial 'START MISSION' label render), so the single most important control is not actually visible/usable in the hero view. The game title is also under-served: 'JS · PLANET / DEFENSE COMMAND' is a tiny header lockup while the largest type on screen is the tagline 'DEFEND THE LAST LIGHT', inverting the intended title hierarchy. CLARITY & HIERARCHY: Focal priority is split and broken — the eye lands on a slogan and a cut-off button rather than a clear title→briefing→CTA→upgrades flow. The right briefing column has a large dead zone below 'TRANSMISSION ENCRYPTED' while the left column is taller, so the two-panel grid reads unbalanced. The 'TOWARD WAVE 1 / T-00:00' card duplicates the header's WAVE 00/12 stat, creating two sources of truth for the same value. The three turret glyphs and the small stat cards (THREAT/SHIELDS/TOWARD) compete with the planet for attention without clear grouping. VISUAL SYSTEM & CRAFT: The thin-stroke, corner-bracket, mono-label HUD language is coherent, but the big flat amber START block violates it — it is a solid slab with no bracketing, bevel, or glow, looking unfinished against the precise line work. The central planet (the thematic hero of a 'Planet Defense' screen) is muddy: low-contrast green blobs on a blue disc with no rim light, crisp shield ring, or legible orbit paths, so the one 'authored' moment is the weakest asset. The background is a near-flat dark field with no starfield, grid, or vignette, giving the 'beautiful sci-fi' brief little atmosphere or depth. Type roles are loose (display headline, mono labels, sans body) without a defined scale, and vertical rhythm in the header stat group (WAVE/HULL/CREDITS) is slightly loose. EXPRESSIVENESS & DISTINCTIVENESS: The command-console identity is competent but generic sci-fi; distinctiveness currently rests on the dashed shield hexagon and the amber accent, both of which are under-executed (muddy planet, flat button). There is no sense of 'live' motion in the static frame (no sweep, pulse, or scan) to justify the 'LIVE / STANDBY' labels. TRADE-OFFS: Making the tagline huge starves the actual title; keeping the CTA huge at the bottom pushes the required upgrades off-screen; adding atmosphere risks cluttering the already dense two-panel grid; investing in the planet competes with investing in the missing upgrade/CTA band. The screen currently optimizes for 'looks like a HUD' over 'fulfills the brief and reads as a polished start screen.'
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan that keeps all required content and resolves the conflicts above. P0 — Fix omissions & clipping (brief + craft): Rebuild the bottom band so it fits the viewport (or is an intentional, fully-rendered section). Render START MISSION as a complete, dominant primary button using the same corner-bracket/scanline language as the panels (amber fill + inner glow + beveled edge + hover/active/focus states), and immediately place the missing upgrade row as three secondary menu buttons — DAMAGE / FIRE RATE / SPEED — each with a small inline SVG icon, label, and credit cost, visually subordinate to START (outline style, not solid). This single band now satisfies the CTA + upgrades requirement and gives the page a clear action zone. P1 — Re-set hierarchy (clarity + intent): Promote the game title to a true hero lockup (large display type 'JS PLANET' with 'DEFENSE COMMAND' as a tracked sub-line) and demote 'DEFEND THE LAST LIGHT' to a one-line tagline directly above the CTA band. This makes the product name the hero and the slogan the support, fixing the inverted hierarchy. Merge the duplicate wave info: keep WAVE in the header as the single source of truth and turn the 'TOWARD WAVE 1' card into a pure countdown or remove it. P2 — Unify the system (craft): Define three explicit type roles (display for title/tagline, mono for all HUD labels/numbers, sans for briefing body) with a fixed scale; give every interactive element (START, upgrades, STANDBY pill) the shared bracket/glow treatment so the flat amber slab becomes part of the system; equalize the two panel heights or fill the right column's dead space (e.g., a small 'last transmission' log or objective checklist) so the grid reads balanced; tighten the gap between the panels and the CTA band. P3 — Strengthen the hero & atmosphere (expressiveness, all CSS/SVG, offline): Re-author the planet as the focal 'defense' asset — crisp disc with atmospheric rim light, a glowing shield hexagon, three distinct turret nodes on visible orbit paths, and a subtle radar sweep; add a faint starfield + low-contrast grid + radial vignette to the background for depth without clutter; add lightweight motion (pulsing STANDBY dot, slow shield shimmer, scan sweep) so the 'LIVE' labels are earned. Net result: title is the hero, briefing is legible, the planet is the memorable authored moment, and the CTA + upgrade row form one clear, fully-visible action system — a polished, on-brief start screen.
